title: Unified trace broker with pluggable sink adapters for vendor integrations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight 'trace broker' service inside the observability backplane that normalizes incoming tracing telemetry and dispatches it to multiple downstream vendors (Tempo, Jaeger, third-party APMs) via pluggable sink adapters. The broker should provide per-tenant routing policies, format normalization (traceid/spanid length alignment, tag translation), backpressure-aware buffering, and TLS/mTLS termination.

Motivation: We currently have per-connector exporters embedded in ingestion pipelines which increases coupling and duplicates logic (sampling, redaction, retry). A centralized broker simplifies connector lifecycle, enables unified policy enforcement (PII redaction, sampling hooks tied to customer config), and makes it easier to add new vendor adapters without touching ingestion hot paths.

Scope:
- Ingest OTLP/HTTP traces from agents/SDKs and internal services.
- Normalize common fields and translate legacy tag formats.
- Support pluggable sink adapters: initial adapters for Tempo and Jaeger-compatible backends, plus a generic HTTP APM adapter.
- Per-tenant routing rules and soft-fallbacks if a sink is unavailable.
- Configurable buffering and priority queueing for SLO-compliant paths.
- Metrics and dashboard hooks for broker health, per-sink latency, queue depth, retry rates, and dropped spans.

Non-goals: Replacing core storage or long-term retention; this is a delivery/dispatch layer. Full schema conversion for vendor-specific proprietary fields will be handled in adapter code rather than the broker itself.
acceptance_criteria: Broker accepts OTLP gRPC and HTTP traces and emits normalized spans to configured sink adapters
Tenant-level routing config can route to 0..N sinks with weighted priorities and fallback rules
Queueing/backpressure prevents head-of-line blocking for high-priority tenant requests
Observability: Prometheus metrics for per-sink latency, queue size, retries, and drop counts visible in console-obs dashboard
Adapters for Tempo and Jaeger testable with end-to-end e2e job and smoke tests running in CI
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Broker becomes a single point of failure. Mitigation: deploy in multi-AZ with leaderless routing and retry on client side; provide circuit-breaker and fail-open options per-tenant
Risk: Increased end-to-end latency due to buffering. Mitigation: prioritize low-latency path for realtime tenants and expose configurable time/size bounds
Risk: Format translation bugs causing downstream loss. Mitigation: comprehensive schema fuzz tests and golden-file traces against test backends
Risk: Secrets for vendor endpoints. Mitigation: use KMS-backed secrets and scoped per-tenant tokens; rotate via ops runbook

2025-02-27: Security review placeholder requested by security team — address mTLS client cert rotation and token scoping

comments: PM feedback (Leah Kim 2025-02-16): Ensure per-tenant SLAs can opt out of buffering and use direct passthrough to vendor for very latency-sensitive customers.
Design feedback (Evan Cho 2025-02-21): Keep adapter interface minimal — provide SendBatch(ctx, []rawSpan) and HealthCheck() to simplify tester mocks.
SRE note (Ravi Singh 2025-02-26): Add an exponential backoff with jitter for transient 5xx from vendor endpoints; surface retry rates on incident runbooks.
Security (Marta Lopez 2025-02-28): Need formal security_review_required sign-off before rolling to prod due to multi-tenant routing of customer traces.
